mistakes.prevent: Raise regulated air until the piston shuttles, which GEARS found takes around 60 psi on new units.

mistakes.title: Passing a one-way F dog
mistakes.what: Accepts an F dog that shuttles to apply but not back to release, or the other way round.
mistakes.consequence: In the vehicle the F dog stays engaged or disengaged, causing P0810-type position faults and missing gears.
mistakes.prevent: Air both the apply and release ports in turn and require full travel each way.

steps.title: Assemble geartrain stack
steps.action: Join planetary sets 3 and 4 in their housing with the C and D hubs, then install the input shaft with A dog and the B drum.

mistakes.title: Dog teeth assembled out of mesh
mistakes.what: Pushes the input shaft with its A dog into the 3-sun/4-ring housing without the dog teeth lined up.
mistakes.consequence: The dog teeth bind tip to tip or chip, so the A dog cannot complete its travel once the unit is running.
mistakes.prevent: Line the teeth up by eye, slide the dog into mesh by hand, and confirm it moves freely before going on.

mistakes.title: Thrust bearing reversed in the stack
mistakes.what: Fits a needle thrust bearing in the geartrain stack upside down.
mistakes.consequence: End play is off, and the bearing runs on the wrong race and breaks up, sending needles through the unit.
mistakes.prevent: Fit each thrust bearing in the orientation recorded on its tag and in the photos.

steps.title: Install C piston and spring
steps.action: Lube the seals, set the aluminum C piston and Belleville spring in the case, compress evenly in the press and fit the snap ring.
steps.why: Uneven compression cuts the piston seals.
steps.mistake: Compressing the spring off-center and rolling a piston seal.

mistakes.title: Off-center C spring compression
mistakes.what: Compresses the C Belleville spring with the press tool off-center.
mistakes.consequence: The C piston tilts and rolls or cuts a seal, so the C brake leaks and slips in the gears where it holds.
mistakes.prevent: Center the press tool on the spring and bring it down slowly and evenly.

mistakes.title: C piston seals fitted dry
mistakes.what: Sets the C piston into its case bore with no lubricant on the seals.
mistakes.consequence: The seals drag and tear as the piston goes in, and the C brake leaks from the first drive.
mistakes.prevent: Coat the C piston seals generously with assembly gel before seating the piston.

mistakes.title: C Belleville spring reversed
mistakes.what: Fits the C Belleville spring upside down.
mistakes.consequence: The C piston no longer releases correctly, so the brake drags and burns or applies harshly.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the spring with the cone facing the way it was marked during teardown.

steps.title: Verify C snap ring seating
steps.action: Release the press and confirm the C snap ring is fully seated in its groove all the way round.
steps.why: FCA issued a bulletin for a C-clutch snap ring on early 948TE units; a half-seated ring here is fatal.

mistakes.title: Half-seated C snap ring
mistakes.what: Releases the press with the C snap ring only partly in its groove.
mistakes.consequence: The ring can work out and leave the C brake stuck on, tying the geartrain up and burning the packs.
mistakes.prevent: Release the press slowly and run a pick around the full ring to confirm it sits in the groove all round.
mistakes.detect: Any spot where the ring's edge stands above the groove wall.

mistakes.title: C ring gap in the old spot
mistakes.what: Fits the new C snap ring with its opening where the original ring's opening was.
mistakes.consequence: The FCA fix places the opening 90 degrees counterclockwise from the original spot, so you lose that improvement.
mistakes.prevent: Mark the original gap position and set the new ring's opening where the bulletin shows.

steps.title: Install C pack and ring
steps.action: Stack the C frictions and steels and install the selective snap ring in the case.

mistakes.title: C frictions installed dry
mistakes.what: Stacks new C frictions straight from the box.
mistakes.consequence: Unsoaked friction material overheats and glazes in the first holds, shortening the life of the new C pack.
mistakes.prevent: Soak each new friction in LifeguardFluid 9 for at least the kit maker's minimum time before stacking.

mistakes.title: Wrong plate count in C
mistakes.what: Builds the C brake with a different number of frictions or steels from the original pack.
mistakes.consequence: Pack thickness changes and the clearance spec for the original disc count no longer applies.
mistakes.prevent: Count the removed plates and match the new pack to that count and order.

steps.title: Check C brake clearance
steps.action: With the specified force on the pack, measure clearance and change the selective snap ring until it is in range.

spec.note: 3-disc pack; 0.020–0.035 in for 2-disc; 45 lb load; selective snap ring (GEARS)

mistakes.title: Wrong C spec for disc count
mistakes.what: Reads C clearance against the 3-disc figure on a 2-disc pack.
mistakes.consequence: The C brake is left outside its true range, so it slips or drags in the gears where it holds.
mistakes.prevent: Count the C frictions and use the clearance range for that disc count.

mistakes.title: Measuring C at one point
mistakes.what: Measures C clearance at one spot around the snap ring.
mistakes.consequence: A cocked pack reads fine at one point and wrong elsewhere, so the selective ring you pick can be off.
mistakes.prevent: Measure at four points around the pack under load and use the average.

steps.title: Seat the number 8 bearing
steps.action: Remove the needle thrust bearing that may still be stuck to the geartrain hub and place it correctly on the oil feed bushing in the case.
steps.why: A bearing left on the hub ends up out of position and wrecks the stack-up.

mistakes.title: Number 8 bearing left on the hub
mistakes.what: Fits the geartrain with the number 8 needle bearing still stuck to its hub.
mistakes.consequence: The bearing lands out of position and is crushed, and every part stacked above it sits wrong.
mistakes.prevent: Pull the bearing off the hub and place it on the oil feed bushing in the case first.

mistakes.title: Number 8 bearing upside down
mistakes.what: Sets the number 8 bearing on the oil feed bushing upside down.
mistakes.consequence: The bearing runs on the wrong face and fails, and input shaft end play comes out wrong.
mistakes.prevent: Match its orientation to the bulletin figure and the tag made at teardown.

steps.title: Install D brake pack
steps.action: Stack the D frictions and steels and line up the friction tabs of the C and D packs.
steps.why: Aligned tabs let the geartrain hubs drop through both packs.

mistakes.title: C and D friction tabs misaligned
mistakes.what: Stacks the D pack without lining its friction tabs up with the C pack below.
mistakes.consequence: The geartrain hubs will not drop through both packs, and forcing them breaks friction tabs.
mistakes.prevent: Line up the C and D friction tabs with a straightedge or by eye before lowering the geartrain.

steps.title: Lower geartrain into case
steps.action: Lower the geartrain by the input shaft and wriggle it until it engages both packs with a solid clunk and the D hub sits just proud of the pack.
steps.why: If the input shaft slips inward or the hubs miss a plate, the stack is wrong and everything above it will be too.
steps.mistake: Forcing the geartrain down without it fully engaging the C and D frictions.

mistakes.title: Forcing the geartrain down
mistakes.what: Pushes the geartrain down before it has engaged both the C and D frictions.
mistakes.consequence: Hubs land on top of the plates, bending tabs, and everything stacked above sits high.
mistakes.prevent: Wriggle the geartrain until it drops with a solid clunk and stop to investigate if it will not.
mistakes.detect: The D hub sits just proud of the D pack once the geartrain is fully down.

mistakes.title: Letting the input shaft slip
mistakes.what: Lets the input shaft slide inward while lowering and wriggling the geartrain.
mistakes.consequence: The B hub and A dog lose their positions, so the stack is wrong before the bell housing even goes on.
mistakes.prevent: Hold the input shaft up firmly while you wriggle and lower the geartrain.

steps.title: Install D piston and retainer
steps.action: Inspect the piston and retainer O-rings, then fit the D Belleville spring, piston and retainer.

mistakes.title: D O-rings fitted unchecked
mistakes.what: Installs the D piston and retainer without looking closely at their O-rings.
mistakes.consequence: A nicked or twisted O-ring leaks D apply oil, and the D brake slips in the gears where it holds.
mistakes.prevent: Inspect each D O-ring under good light and replace any that are marked, flattened or twisted.

mistakes.title: Retainer O-ring in the ring groove
mistakes.what: Lowers the D retainer without watching its O-ring.
mistakes.consequence: The O-ring drops into the snap ring groove and is cut when the ring goes in.
mistakes.prevent: Gel the O-ring so it stays put and watch it go past the groove as the retainer comes down.

steps.title: Compress D retainer, fit ring
steps.action: Compress the D retainer in the press until the groove shows and install its snap ring.
steps.why: Only once the retainer is locked down can the D clearance be measured and the transfer gear bearing go back on.

mistakes.title: D retainer ring partly seated
mistakes.what: Releases the press with the tabless D snap ring only partly in its groove.
mistakes.consequence: The retainer can pop out under apply pressure and the D brake loses apply oil.
mistakes.prevent: Run a pick around the whole ring before releasing the press and confirm it is fully seated.

mistakes.title: Pressing the D retainer too far
mistakes.what: Keeps pressing the D retainer after its snap ring groove is exposed.
mistakes.consequence: The retainer or Belleville spring distorts, changing how the D piston applies.
mistakes.prevent: Press only until the groove shows, which is a small amount of travel.

steps.title: Check D brake clearance
steps.action: With the specified force applied, measure D clearance and change the selective backing plate if it is out of range.

mistakes.title: Skipping the two-step D check
mistakes.what: Tries to feeler-gauge the D pack instead of the two-step measurement.
mistakes.consequence: There is no clean gap to measure, so the D clearance ends up guessed and outside its range.
mistakes.prevent: Measure case lug to snap ring, then the loaded pack thickness, and subtract.

mistakes.title: Shimming D with the snap ring
mistakes.what: Tries to correct D clearance by swapping its snap ring.
mistakes.consequence: D clearance is set by a selective backing plate, so the clearance does not change.
mistakes.prevent: Change the selective backing plate to bring D clearance into range.

steps.title: Press on transfer gear bearing
steps.action: Press the transfer gear bearing back onto its case boss.
steps.why: It goes back only after the D piston retainer is in, because it blocks the retainer.

mistakes.title: Pressing the bearing through its rollers
mistakes.what: Presses the transfer gear bearing on by pushing on its outer race or cage.
mistakes.consequence: The load passes through the rollers and dents the races, so the bearing whines in service.
mistakes.prevent: Press only on the inner race with a driver that clears the cage.

mistakes.title: Bearing fitted before the D retainer
mistakes.what: Presses the transfer gear bearing on before the D piston retainer is locked in.
mistakes.consequence: The bearing blocks the retainer, so it has to be pulled again and may be damaged.
mistakes.prevent: Lock the D retainer in with its snap ring before pressing the bearing on.

steps.title: Install lower annulus and carrier
steps.action: Install the gear 3 annulus and carrier assembly.

mistakes.title: Thrust washer left out between sets
mistakes.what: Installs the lower annulus and carrier with a thrust washer missing.
mistakes.consequence: Gears rub where the washer should be, and end play and wear go wrong.
mistakes.prevent: Check every tagged washer and bearing is in the stack before lowering each assembly.

steps.title: Install upper annulus and carrier
steps.action: Install the gear 4 annulus and pinion carrier assembly.

mistakes.title: Upper carrier sitting high
mistakes.what: Leaves the upper annulus and carrier sitting high instead of fully engaged.
mistakes.consequence: The output support and E clutch above will not line up, and the bell housing will not seat.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the carrier until it drops fully and compare its height with the teardown photos.

steps.title: Fit output support on carrier
steps.action: Set the output gear support onto the carrier with its lower teeth fully meshed and its tube orifices lined up.
steps.why: Misaligned orifices block the oblong tubes that feed the F dog.
steps.mistake: Setting the support down a tooth off so the tube orifices do not line up.

mistakes.title: Output support a tooth off
mistakes.what: Sets the output gear support onto the carrier with its tube orifices out of line.
mistakes.consequence: The oblong tubes cannot feed the support, so the F dog is starved and will not move.
mistakes.prevent: Line up the tube orifices with the case tube positions before you seat the support.

mistakes.title: Output support teeth half-meshed
mistakes.what: Leaves the output support's lower teeth only partly meshed with the carrier.
mistakes.consequence: The support sits high and the bell housing is pulled down onto it.
mistakes.prevent: Check the lower teeth are fully engaged before you go on.

steps.title: Install E clutch onto support
steps.action: Holding the E plates in their hub, set the E clutch and hub onto the output gear support.

mistakes.title: E plates dropping from the hub
mistakes.what: Moves the E clutch and hub onto the support without holding the plates in place.
mistakes.consequence: Plates slip out of the hub, and the bell housing will not seat over a misaligned E pack.
mistakes.prevent: Hold the E plates in their hub with your fingers while setting the assembly down.

steps.title: Install transfer gear and differential
steps.action: Install the transfer gear on its bearing meshed with the output gear, then the differential meshed with the transfer pinion.
steps.why: Reverse of removal: the transfer gear must be in before the differential can mesh with it.

mistakes.title: Differential before the transfer gear
mistakes.what: Drops the differential in before the transfer gear is on its bearing.
mistakes.consequence: The transfer gear can no longer go in meshed with both gears, so the differential has to come out again.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the transfer gear meshed with the output gear first, then the differential.

steps.title: Fit tube seal and gasket
steps.action: Install a new fluid port tube seal in the case and lay a new bell housing gasket on the case face.
steps.mistake: Leaving out the new tube seal between case and bell housing.

mistakes.title: Leaving out the new tube seal
mistakes.what: Lays the bell housing gasket down and forgets the new fluid port tube seal.
mistakes.consequence: Oil leaks between case and bell housing at that port, and fixing it means splitting the unit again.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the tube seal first and tick it off on the job card before the gasket goes down.

mistakes.title: Reusing the bell housing gasket
mistakes.what: Puts the old rubber-coated steel bell housing gasket back.
mistakes.consequence: The case-to-converter-housing joint, a JLR-listed leak point, seeps fluid until the unit runs low.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new bell housing gasket every time the housing is split.

mistakes.title: Tube seal standing proud
mistakes.what: Leaves the new tube seal sitting above its bore.
mistakes.consequence: The bell housing crushes the seal as it comes down, and that port leaks even though the seal is new.
mistakes.prevent: Press the seal fully home and check it is flush before the housing goes on.

steps.title: Lower bell housing onto case
steps.action: Lower the bell housing over the stack, rotating the output support and E clutch slightly until the guide pins enter their holes.
steps.why: Grease on the stator support rings keeps them from being cut as the E drum slides on.

mistakes.title: Cutting stator support rings
mistakes.what: Lowers the bell housing with the stator support sealing rings dry.
mistakes.consequence: The E drum slices the rings as it slides on, and the E clutch leaks apply oil in 4th to 9th.
mistakes.prevent: Grease the stator support rings so they stay sized and centred as the E drum slides over them.

mistakes.title: Forcing the housing past its pins
mistakes.what: Pushes the bell housing down when it hangs up instead of turning the output support and E clutch.
mistakes.consequence: Tubes, rings or the support teeth are crushed between housing and case.
mistakes.prevent: Rotate the output support and E clutch slightly until the guide pins drop into their holes by weight alone.

mistakes.title: Gasket shifting off its dowels
mistakes.what: Lowers the bell housing without checking the gasket is still on its dowels.
mistakes.consequence: A shifted gasket pinches under the flange and the joint leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Check the gasket sits flat on its dowels just before the housing comes down.

steps.title: Torque bell housing bolts
steps.action: Run all bolts in by hand, torque the inner bolts in their sequence, then the outer perimeter bolts in theirs.
steps.why: Inner bolts first pulls the housing down evenly over the output support and E clutch.

spec.note: inner then outer, each in sequence; 948TE figure from FCA TSB, confirm for the JLR unit

mistakes.title: Outer bell bolts torqued first
mistakes.what: Torques the outer perimeter bolts before the inner bolts.
mistakes.consequence: The housing is pulled down unevenly over the output support and E clutch, risking binding and a weeping joint.
mistakes.prevent: Hand-start all the bolts, then torque the inner bolts in sequence before the outer ones.

mistakes.title: Using the 948TE torque unchecked
mistakes.what: Uses the FCA 948TE bell housing torque figure without checking it for the JLR unit.
mistakes.consequence: If the JLR value differs, the joint ends up over- or under-clamped.
mistakes.prevent: Check the torque in the JLR or ZF data and note which figure you used.

mistakes.title: Bell bolt in the wrong hole
mistakes.what: Starts a bell housing bolt in a hole meant for a different length.
mistakes.consequence: A long bolt bottoms before clamping and a short one pulls threads out of the aluminium case.
mistakes.prevent: Take bolts from the hole-pattern template one at a time.

steps.title: Check input shaft end play
steps.action: Check the input shaft end play and that the shaft turns with slight resistance.
steps.why: Zero end play or a bound shaft means a misplaced bearing or a hub not fully engaged; open it now, not after fill.

mistakes.title: Skipping the end play check
mistakes.what: Moves on to the valve body without checking input shaft end play.
mistakes.consequence: A misplaced thrust bearing or unseated hub goes unnoticed until the unit is installed and filled.
mistakes.prevent: Check end play and that the shaft turns with slight resistance before any more parts go on.

mistakes.title: Ignoring a bound input shaft
mistakes.what: Notes that the input shaft is tight or will not turn and carries on.
mistakes.consequence: A hub is sitting on a plate instead of engaged, which burns that pack on the first drive.
mistakes.prevent: Split the housing now and find the hub that has not engaged.

steps.title: Drive in new differential seals
steps.action: Drive new differential seals into the case and bell housing with the seal installer.
steps.why: With the housing bolted up, the seals can be driven square against a fully supported bore.

mistakes.title: Differential seal driven cocked
mistakes.what: Drives a differential seal in at an angle.
mistakes.consequence: The lip runs off-centre on the halfshaft and leaks fluid at the axle.
mistakes.prevent: Use the correct seal installer and drive the seal square against its stop.

mistakes.title: Not checking the sealing plug
mistakes.what: Closes up without checking the right-hand internal differential sealing plug.
mistakes.consequence: If the plug is missing, the transmission-to-differential joint leaks once the PTU is fitted.
mistakes.prevent: Confirm the plug is in place before the PTU goes on.
mistakes.detect: The differential cross pin is visible through the bore when the plug is missing.

steps.title: Install connecting tubes
steps.action: Install the valve body connecting tubes in the case with new O-rings, with the two oblong tubes turned the right way.
steps.mistake: Fitting an oblong tube rotated so it starves the output support circuit.

mistakes.title: Oblong tube turned wrong
mistakes.what: Fits an oblong connecting tube rotated from its recorded position.
mistakes.consequence: The tube blocks the output support circuit, so the F dog is starved and will not move.
mistakes.prevent: Turn each oblong tube to match the teardown photos before pressing it home.

mistakes.title: Cutting tube O-rings on entry
mistakes.what: Pushes connecting tubes into the case with dry new O-rings.
mistakes.consequence: An O-ring is sliced on the bore edge and that circuit leaks under pressure.
mistakes.prevent: Lube each O-ring lightly and push the tubes in straight.

mistakes.title: Leaving a connecting tube out
mistakes.what: Installs the connecting tubes from memory and misses one.
mistakes.consequence: The circuit it feeds has no supply, so its element will not apply at all.
mistakes.prevent: Check the tube count against the list made at teardown before fitting the valve body.

steps.title: Fit large tubes to valve body
steps.action: Install the two larger transfer tubes and the filter bypass tube into the valve body with new O-rings.
steps.why: The bypass tube gives instant pressure on restart after an auto stop; a leak here shows as slow drive-away.

mistakes.title: Bypass tube missing or leaking
mistakes.what: Leaves out the filter bypass tube or fits it with an old O-ring.
mistakes.consequence: Drive-away is slow after an engine auto stop, because the bypass that gives fast pressure on restart is missing.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the bypass tube with new O-rings and tick it off with the other tubes.

mistakes.title: Rolled O-ring on a large tube
mistakes.what: Pushes one of the large transfer tubes into the valve body with a rolled O-ring.
mistakes.consequence: The tube leaks a high-flow circuit, dropping pressure to the elements it feeds.
mistakes.prevent: Lube the O-ring and push the tube in straight, checking the ring is not twisted.

steps.title: Bolt in range and speed sensors
steps.action: With the valve body held over the case, install the range sensor and speed sensor and torque their bolts.

mistakes.title: Overtightened sensor bolts
mistakes.what: Tightens the range and speed sensor bolts by feel with a long ratchet.
mistakes.consequence: These small bolts take a low torque, so the threads in the case strip or the sensor body cracks.
mistakes.prevent: Torque the sensor bolts to the small figure in the service data with a suitable wrench.

mistakes.title: Sensor harness pinched underneath
mistakes.what: Lets the sensor harness slip under the valve body while fitting the sensors.
mistakes.consequence: The wire is crushed as the valve body seats and range or speed codes follow.
mistakes.prevent: Route the harness clear and hold it aside while lowering the valve body.

steps.title: Seat valve body on tubes
steps.action: Line the valve body up over the tubes, guide the manual lever cam into the manual valve slot, and press it into place evenly.
steps.mistake: Missing the manual valve slot so park and gear selection are wrong.

mistakes.title: Missing the manual valve slot
mistakes.what: Seats the valve body with the manual lever cam beside the manual valve slot instead of in it.
mistakes.consequence: The valve body ignores the selector, so Park and gear selection are wrong and the cam can break.
mistakes.prevent: Guide the cam into the slot before pressing the valve body down and check the lever moves the valve.

mistakes.title: Bolting the valve body down
mistakes.what: Uses the valve body bolts to pull it down onto the connecting tubes.
mistakes.consequence: The valve body cocks on the tubes, cutting O-rings and possibly cracking the casting.
mistakes.prevent: Press the valve body on evenly by hand until it sits flat, then fit the bolts.

steps.title: Torque valve body bolts
steps.action: Install the valve body bolts and torque them in sequence.

spec.note: in sequence; 948TE figure from FCA TSB

mistakes.title: Valve body torqued out of sequence
mistakes.what: Torques the valve body bolts in no particular order.
mistakes.consequence: The casting distorts and valves bind in their bores, causing sticky or erratic shifts.
mistakes.prevent: Torque the bolts in the published sequence, in stages.

mistakes.title: Valve body bolts swapped by length
mistakes.what: Puts a long valve body bolt in a short hole.
mistakes.consequence: The bolt bottoms out without clamping, or pushes into a passage and cracks the valve body.
mistakes.prevent: Take each bolt from its slot in the template and check its length before starting it.

mistakes.title: Stripping valve body threads
mistakes.what: Overshoots the valve body bolt torque with an uncalibrated wrench.
mistakes.consequence: Threads in the aluminium case pull out and need thread inserts before the valve body can be clamped.
mistakes.prevent: Use a calibrated small-range torque wrench for every valve body bolt.

steps.title: Refit side cover and connector
steps.action: Lube the connector O-rings, set the side cover on, push the connector through until the clip groove shows, fit the clip and torque the cover bolts.

mistakes.title: Reusing the side cover gasket
mistakes.what: Puts the side cover back on its old molded gasket.
mistakes.consequence: JLR traced a leak with poor shifts and noise to this gasket, so the cover weeps and the level falls.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the new ZF cover gasket kit every time the cover comes off.

mistakes.title: Connector O-rings fitted dry
mistakes.what: Pushes the case connector through the cover with dry O-rings.
mistakes.consequence: The O-rings roll or tear and fluid wicks out through the connector.
mistakes.prevent: Give the connector O-rings a light coat of assembly lube before fitting.

mistakes.title: Clip fitted before the groove shows
mistakes.what: Fits the connector clip without pushing the connector far enough to expose its groove.
mistakes.consequence: The clip does not lock, so the connector backs out and intermittent electrical faults follow.
mistakes.prevent: Push the connector until the full clip groove shows, then fit the clip.

mistakes.title: Overtightening the plastic cover
mistakes.what: Tightens the cover bolts hard where a torque limiter is missing.
mistakes.consequence: The plastic side cover cracks at a bolt boss and leaks there.
mistakes.prevent: Check every limiter is present and torque the bolts to the cover figure.

steps.title: Install oil gallery plate
steps.action: Fit the oil passage cover with a new gasket and new bolts, tightening them in sequence.

spec.note: new bolts, in sequence (Evoque 9HP48 data via PMM/Autodata)

mistakes.title: Reusing gallery plate bolts
mistakes.what: Refits the oil gallery plate with its original bolts.
mistakes.consequence: The bolts may not clamp the plate evenly and the bonded gasket weeps at a known leak point.
mistakes.prevent: Fit new gallery plate bolts as the repair data calls for.

mistakes.title: Gallery plate tightened out of order
mistakes.what: Tightens the gallery plate bolts in no particular order.
mistakes.consequence: The plate pulls down unevenly and leaks, causing low fluid, noise and poor shifts.
mistakes.prevent: Tighten the bolts in the published sequence to the specified torque.

mistakes.title: Reusing the bonded gallery gasket
mistakes.what: Puts the old bonded steel gasket back under the gallery plate.
mistakes.consequence: This gasket was a known Evoque fault on its own; a used one leaks at once.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new bonded gasket every time the plate comes off.

steps.title: Refit external line and TCM
steps.action: Install the external hydraulic line with new seals and bolt the TCM back onto the case.

mistakes.title: Reusing external line seals
mistakes.what: Refits the external hydraulic line on its old seals.
mistakes.consequence: The line weeps or blows off under pressure and the unit loses fluid fast on the road.
mistakes.prevent: Fit new seals to the external line and check its ends seat squarely.

steps.title: Fully engage torque converter
steps.action: Slide the converter on while turning it until it drops through each engagement and the hub's flats engage the pump drive gear.
steps.why: A converter that is not fully seated is pulled into the pump when the bolts are tightened.
steps.mistake: Bolting up a converter that has only engaged the input shaft and not the pump drive.

mistakes.title: Converter on the input shaft only
mistakes.what: Slides the converter on until it stops at the first engagement.
mistakes.consequence: Bolting it to the flexplate drives the hub into the pump drive gear and pump, wrecking the pump and filling the new unit with debris.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the converter while pushing until it drops through each engagement and the hub flats engage the pump drive.
mistakes.detect: The converter turns freely and sits back from the bell housing face as far as the service data calls for.

mistakes.title: Not measuring converter set-back
mistakes.what: Installs the unit without measuring how far the converter sits back in the bell housing.
mistakes.consequence: A converter that has missed its last engagement looks fine by eye and goes in unnoticed.
mistakes.prevent: Measure from the bell housing face to the converter mounting pads and compare with the service figure.

mistakes.title: Folding the new hub seal lip
mistakes.what: Slides the converter in with a dry hub.
mistakes.consequence: The new converter hub seal lip folds over and the unit leaks at the converter from the first start.
mistakes.prevent: Lube the converter hub and slide it in straight without rocking it.

steps.title: Install transmission to engine
steps.action: Raise the unit, engage the dowels, and torque the transmission-to-engine bolts.

spec.note: ±7.5 N·m for the M10 transmission-to-engine bolt in JLR SSM72569 (16MY GTDi); confirm for Ingenium

mistakes.title: Drawing the case up with bolts
mistakes.what: Uses the transmission-to-engine bolts to pull the unit the last distance onto the engine.
mistakes.consequence: If the converter or a dowel is not lined up, the bolts crack the bell housing or force the converter into the pump.
mistakes.prevent: Bring the unit fully flush on the dowels by hand before fitting any bolt.

mistakes.title: Reusing a flagged engine bolt
mistakes.what: Reuses a transmission-to-engine bolt that a JLR bulletin says to replace on certain VINs.
mistakes.consequence: On the affected 16MY vehicles the old bolt can strip the oil pan thread when reinstalled.
mistakes.prevent: Check bulletins for your VIN and fit the replacement bolt they specify.

mistakes.title: Not spinning the converter after bolting
mistakes.what: Moves straight on to the converter nuts without turning the converter by hand.
mistakes.consequence: A converter that is binding against the pump drive goes unnoticed until it damages the pump.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the converter by hand after the bell housing bolts are tight and stop if it binds.

steps.title: Fit converter with new nuts
steps.action: Line up the converter marks and fit new flexplate-to-converter nuts, torqued to spec.
steps.mistake: Reusing the old converter nuts.

mistakes.title: Old converter nuts refitted
mistakes.what: Refits the flexplate-to-converter nuts that came off at removal.
mistakes.consequence: The converter is held by fixings JLR says must be renewed, risking a loose converter and a second removal.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the new flexplate-to-converter nuts that JLR specifies and torque them to spec.

mistakes.title: Converter pads not flat
mistakes.what: Tightens one converter nut fully while the pads are not sitting flat on the flexplate.
mistakes.consequence: The converter is drawn out of line and loads the pump drive and hub seal off-centre.
mistakes.prevent: Check all pads touch the flexplate, snug every nut, then torque them in turn.

steps.title: Refit PTU, shafts and lines
steps.action: Refit the PTU to the differential side with a new seal, the halfshafts, cooler lines, harness and selector.
steps.why: The transmission-to-PTU joint is a listed leak point; a dry seal here empties the transmission.

mistakes.title: Superseded PTU interface parts
mistakes.what: Refits the PTU with quill shaft seals and clips from an old stock kit.
mistakes.consequence: JLR revised these clips because the earlier ones let the quill shaft and seals assemble wrong and leak.
mistakes.prevent: Order the latest quill shaft seals and clips from the parts catalogue and follow the current procedure.

mistakes.title: Filling the PTU with ATF
mistakes.what: Tops up or refills the PTU with the transmission's ATF.
mistakes.consequence: The PTU uses its own gear oil, so ATF in it shortens the life of its gears and bearings.
mistakes.prevent: Fill the PTU with its own specified oil, separately from the transmission.

mistakes.title: Fitting a dirty oil cooler
mistakes.what: Reconnects the oil cooler and lines without flushing them after a failure that made debris.
mistakes.consequence: Debris trapped in the cooler starves the new unit of lube flow, a leading cause of repeat failures.
mistakes.prevent: Back-flush, forward-flush and back-flush the cooler and lines, or replace the cooler.

mistakes.title: Cooler joint not fully seated
mistakes.what: Connects the cooler to the transmission without checking the joint is fully home.
mistakes.consequence: The cooler-to-housing joint, a JLR-listed leak point, seeps and lowers the level.
mistakes.prevent: Seat the joint fully with new seals and check it before filling.

steps.title: Fill with LifeguardFluid 9
steps.action: Fill through the fill port with ZF LifeguardFluid 9 (JLR part LR023288) to an initial level; do not mix in other fluids or leak dye.
steps.why: Other fluids change friction behavior and shift feel on this unit.

spec.note: approximate total capacity from a capacity database; final level is set hot

steps.mistake: Topping up with a generic multi-vehicle ATF.

mistakes.title: Topping up with generic ATF
mistakes.what: Fills with a generic multi-vehicle ATF instead of ZF LifeguardFluid 9.
mistakes.consequence: Different friction behaviour changes how the clutches apply, giving poor shift quality and faster wear.
mistakes.prevent: Use ZF LifeguardFluid 9 (JLR LR023288) and nothing else.

mistakes.title: Adding additives or cleaners
mistakes.what: Adds a friction modifier, conditioner or flush chemical to the new fluid.
mistakes.consequence: ZF warns these alter the oil's chemistry, which upsets clutch apply on a freshly built unit.
mistakes.prevent: Fill with plain LifeguardFluid 9 and add nothing to it.

mistakes.title: Starting the engine empty
mistakes.what: Cranks or starts the engine before any fluid is in the transmission.
mistakes.consequence: The pump runs dry and the new parts turn without oil.
mistakes.prevent: Put the initial fill in before the engine is started or the vehicle is moved.

steps.title: Update and configure TCM
steps.action: Connect a battery support unit and the JLR diagnostic tool, update the TCM to the latest calibration and run the TCM configure routine, entering the transmission serial number when asked.
steps.why: The TCM is matched to the transmission; the routine asks for the serial number.

mistakes.title: Entering the wrong serial
mistakes.what: Mistypes the transmission serial number when the configure routine asks for it.
mistakes.consequence: JLR's bulletin warns that not following this routine correctly can lead to serious mechanical failure.
mistakes.prevent: Enter the serial from the label photo and have someone check the digits before confirming.

mistakes.title: Programming without battery support
mistakes.what: Flashes the TCM on the vehicle battery alone.
mistakes.consequence: A voltage drop mid-flash can corrupt the module, adding a replacement TCM to the job.
mistakes.prevent: Connect a JLR-approved battery support unit before starting the session.

mistakes.title: Skipping ignition prompts
mistakes.what: Clicks through the diagnostic tool's ignition-on and ignition-off requests without acting on them.
mistakes.consequence: JLR warns that skipping these ignition steps can damage control modules during programming.
mistakes.prevent: Carry out every ignition request exactly when the tool asks for it.

steps.title: Set level at temperature
steps.action: With the engine idling in park, monitor fluid temperature on the diagnostic tool and set the level at the check plug within the temperature window in the service data.
steps.why: The level changes with temperature; a level set cold or too hot is wrong.
steps.mistake: Setting the level by volume alone without the hot check.

mistakes.title: Setting the level by fill volume
mistakes.what: Puts in the approximate capacity and skips the hot level check.
mistakes.consequence: Too little fluid has left this family with no forward gear, and too much causes its own damage.
mistakes.prevent: Set the final level at the check plug within the specified temperature window.

mistakes.title: Checking the level too hot
mistakes.what: Sets the level after a long drive with the fluid above the window.
mistakes.consequence: Hot fluid has expanded, so a level set then is low once it cools to the check temperature.
mistakes.prevent: Let the fluid cool into the window and recheck on the scan tool.

mistakes.title: Auto stop during the check
mistakes.what: Leaves start-stop enabled and the engine shuts off while you check the level.
mistakes.consequence: The check is made with the pump stopped instead of idling, so the reading is wrong.
mistakes.prevent: Turn start-stop off before checking so the engine keeps idling.

mistakes.title: Not cycling the selector first
mistakes.what: Checks the level without first shifting through R and D at idle.
mistakes.consequence: Oil has not yet filled the circuits and converter, so the level drops after you close the plug.
mistakes.prevent: Move through R and D with the brake on, return to P, then check.

steps.title: Reset and relearn adaptations
steps.action: Clear the transmission adaptation values and run the guided adaptation procedure.
steps.why: Adaptations are learned clutch fill times and pressures; old values from worn parts give harsh or flared shifts on the new packs.
steps.mistake: Skipping the adaptation reset and blaming the rebuild for harsh shifts.

mistakes.title: Skipping the adaptation reset
mistakes.what: Drives off on the adaptation values the TCM learned on the worn parts.
mistakes.consequence: Fill times learned on worn packs suit the new ones badly, giving harsh or flared shifts.
mistakes.prevent: Clear the adaptations and run the guided adaptation routine.

mistakes.title: Learning with codes stored
mistakes.what: Starts the adaptation routine with transmission codes still stored.
mistakes.consequence: The learn is built on a faulty input, or refused, and shift quality does not improve.
mistakes.prevent: Diagnose and clear every TCM code, then run the learn.

mistakes.title: Learning with cold fluid
mistakes.what: Runs the adaptation learn straight after the first start with the fluid still cool.
mistakes.consequence: The routine needs a minimum fluid temperature, so values learned cold are wrong.
mistakes.prevent: Drive until the scan tool shows the fluid temperature the routine requires, then learn.

mistakes.title: Start-stop on during the learn
mistakes.what: Leaves start-stop enabled while running the learn.
mistakes.consequence: Auto stops interrupt the learn events, leaving the adaptation values incomplete.
mistakes.prevent: Turn start-stop off before starting the learn and keep it off until it finishes.

mistakes.title: Running the wrong learn routine
mistakes.what: Runs a valve body or solenoid learn when only an adaptation learn is needed.
mistakes.consequence: On this family that routine wipes factory settings as well as adaptations, leaving shifts worse.
mistakes.prevent: Choose the routine that matches the repair: adaptations after an overhaul, solenoid learn only after valve body or TCM replacement.

steps.title: Road test all gears
steps.action: Drive through every upshift and downshift to ninth, including part-throttle and kickdown, and check engagements from park to reverse to drive.
steps.why: Dog clutch engagements need several cycles before shifts settle.

mistakes.title: Judging after a few shifts
mistakes.what: Rates shift quality on the first handful of shifts.
mistakes.consequence: Clutches need repeated shift events before they settle, so the rebuild looks bad when it is not.
mistakes.prevent: Repeat each upshift and downshift several times before rating them.

mistakes.title: Not repeating P-R-D engagements
mistakes.what: Checks the Park to Reverse to Drive engagements only once.
mistakes.consequence: A dog clutch that hangs up intermittently, such as at startup, slips past the test.
mistakes.prevent: Cycle P, R and D several times, hot and cold, and rescan after each set.

steps.title: Recheck codes, leaks, level
steps.action: Rescan for codes, inspect the cover, case joint, cooler and PTU joint for leaks, and recheck the hot level.

mistakes.title: Skipping the post-test leak check
mistakes.what: Hands the vehicle back without rechecking the cover, case joint, cooler and PTU joint.
mistakes.consequence: A small seep empties the unit over the next weeks, leading to dog clutch faults or no drive.
mistakes.prevent: Inspect all four listed joints after the road test with the case cleaned beforehand.

mistakes.title: Not rechecking the hot level
mistakes.what: Trusts the level set before the road test.
mistakes.consequence: Once the cooler and circuits have filled, the level drops below the check plug.
mistakes.prevent: Recheck the level at temperature after the road test and top up.

mistakes.title: Clearing new codes unread
mistakes.what: Clears post-test codes without recording them.
mistakes.consequence: A code from the first drive is the earliest warning of a rebuild error, and it is lost.
mistakes.prevent: Save and read every code after the road test before clearing anything.

failureModes.title: A dog clutch failure (no forward or lost gears)
failureModes.cause: The A dog on the input shaft stops completing its travel: a loose or broken sensing plate screw, worn sleeve or splines, or a sensing valve problem.
symptoms: Loss of forward gears or higher gears
Grinding or ratcheting on engagement
Dog clutch position codes such as P0810
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Inspect the A dog splines and both halves of the joint, check the sensing screw, air-test full travel and replace the input shaft assembly with the correct variant if any check fails (zf-9hp48-052, -053, -054, -078).

failureModes.title: Stuck in Park or drops back to Park
failureModes.cause: The dog clutch position check fails at startup, from a sticking A dog, a failed dog pressure sensor or park system wear; body signals such as a door ajar can also hold Park.
symptoms: Vehicle will not leave Park or returns to Park after selecting R or D
P0810 clutch position control error
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Rule out body codes during diagnosis, then check A dog freedom, bench-test the Hall-effect pressure sensor and inspect the park pawl, gear and rod (zf-9hp48-001, -054, -056, -062).

failureModes.title: Worn A/F dog plunger valve sleeves
failureModes.cause: The valve plungers reciprocate in aluminium sleeves and wear them, so dog clutch pressure overlaps or exhausts early.
symptoms: Delayed engagement
Loss of higher gears
RPM cycling during shifts
Damaged A or F dog teeth
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Inspect the sleeves at teardown and fit the plunger kit that matches the park-by-wire or park-by-cable valve body (zf-9hp48-057, -066).

failureModes.title: Line pressure control wear
failureModes.cause: Oscillating wear in the pressure regulator bore and the SV-SP valve bore that feeds it lets regulated oil escape.
symptoms: Low, high or erratic line pressure
Poor shift quality
Burnt clutches
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Vacuum-test the regulator and SV-SP bores and ream and fit oversize valves where they fail (zf-9hp48-057, -066).

failureModes.title: Low fluid from cover gasket leaks
failureModes.cause: The side cover gasket was damaged in manufacture on some units, letting fluid leak until the level drops.
symptoms: Visible leak at the side cover
Poor shift quality and transmission noise
TCM codes such as P2545/P2546 that clear once the leak and level are fixed
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Fit the new ZF cover gasket kit whenever the cover is off and set the level hot (zf-9hp48-002, -013, -105, -114).

failureModes.title: Oil gallery plate gasket leak
failureModes.cause: The bonded steel gasket under the oil passage cover plate was a known manufacturing fault on the 9HP48.
symptoms: Fluid leak from the case
Poor gear shifting
Abnormal transmission noise
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Fit a new bonded gasket and new bolts, tightened in sequence (zf-9hp48-019, -106).

failureModes.title: PTU interface and differential plug leaks
failureModes.cause: Quill shaft seals and clips at the PTU joint can assemble wrong, and the internal differential sealing plug is knocked out when halfshafts are pushed through.
symptoms: Oil leaking from the front of the vehicle at the PTU joint
Fluid level dropping after a driveline repair
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Pull halfshafts from the outboard side, confirm the sealing plug is present, and fit the latest PTU interface seals and clips (zf-9hp48-006, -099, -111).

failureModes.title: Underfill leading to no drive
failureModes.cause: The transmission runs short of fluid, from a fill set by volume or a leak, and the elements cannot apply.
symptoms: No forward gear
Slipping or delayed engagements
Dog clutch codes
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Set the level at the check plug inside the temperature window, then recheck after the road test (zf-9hp48-112, -114, -117).

failureModes.title: Early calibration shift complaints
failureModes.cause: First-generation TCM software gave harsh or delayed shifts, irregular gear changes or neutral selection, much of it fixed by later calibrations.
symptoms: Harsh upshifts and downshifts
Delayed engagements
Irregular shift or neutral selected, P1758
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Update the TCM, configure it to the transmission serial and relearn adaptations before and after any repair (zf-9hp48-003, -113, -115).

failureModes.title: Internal harness crimp failure
failureModes.cause: Insufficient crimps in the transmission wiring harness on some early units broke contact intermittently.
symptoms: Sudden shift to neutral and loss of drive
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Check the vehicle for the recall, and inspect and pull-test the terminals at the connector plate during the rebuild (zf-9hp48-001, -063).

failureModes.title: C brake snap ring dislodging
failureModes.cause: On early 948TE units of the same design the C piston snap ring could dislodge; FCA fitted a new ring with its gap moved.
symptoms: C element stuck-on code (P07A7 on the 948TE)
Tie-up or harsh engagements
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Fit a new C snap ring with its gap where the bulletin shows and check it is seated all round (zf-9hp48-065, -080).

failureModes.title: External hydraulic line blowout
failureModes.cause: The external hydraulic line at the back of the case ages and can blow out.
symptoms: Sudden fluid loss under the vehicle
Loss of drive once the level drops
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Inspect the line and renew its seals on every overhaul (zf-9hp48-020, -107).

failureModes.title: Converter lockup wear and contamination
failureModes.cause: Lockup is used in every gear, so the converter clutch wears, and debris from a failure collects inside the converter.
symptoms: Shudder under light throttle
Repeat contamination of a rebuilt unit
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Send the converter out or replace it after a debris-making failure, and seat it fully on install (zf-9hp48-064, -108).

failureModes.title: Repeat failure from a dirty cooler
failureModes.cause: Debris from the original failure stays in the oil cooler and lines and restricts lube flow to the new unit.
symptoms: Early wear or failure of a freshly rebuilt transmission
Debris back in the fluid soon after the rebuild
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Note debris at the drain and flush or replace the cooler before the rebuilt unit runs (zf-9hp48-005, -111).
